analysis.title: Rates Spark: Back to a 5% 10Y UST on inflation fears
key_insights: US core CPI printed 0.3% MoM, which annualises to well above 3% and is far from the Fed's target. ING calls the move in the 10Y UST yield back to 5% justified.
Last week's solid payrolls report gives the Fed little reason to take a more dovish path for now. Energy prices and AI investment add further inflation uncertainty.

Fed Governor Waller said he backs a 25bp hike in December and could opt for 50bp. After his comments the 10yr yield rose 6bp and the 2yr rose 13bp. Markets now price more than a full 25bp hike in December, versus 20bp before Waller spoke. ING's own forecast is a 25bp hike.
Hopes of Middle East de-escalation are pulling energy costs lower. Retail gasoline is below $4/gallon for the first time since mid-July, which should help a subdued November CPI print.
November CPI will not be released until the day after the December FOMC meeting. ING expects the Fed may get a sneak peek, which should give it the confidence to raise only 25bp.
ING forecasts no further Fed hikes in 2027. It expects rate-sensitive sectors to cool, with housing costs and lower energy prices amid weak wage growth dampening price pressures.
EUR and GBP rates followed the Fed's hawkish repricing, but ING thinks those moves could fade fast. The 2Y EUR inflation swap fell on the day, so the spillover was purely in real rates.

ING argues the US and Europe face different inflation paths. Europe is more exposed to energy prices and the US to AI-related growth. Tight US-Europe rate correlation is warranted if oil drives it, but less so if US macro data does.

Higher US rates tighten financial conditions for Europe, so the ECB or Bank of England may not need to hike as aggressively as priced. Many ECB speakers have linked higher long-dated rates to a reduced need to raise policy rates.
ING prefers to focus on European inflation data and not be carried away by US CPI surprises.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The report calls it an upside surprise. Annualised it is well above 3%, far from the Fed's target, and it sent Treasury yields sharply higher.
The yield returned to 5% after the CPI surprise and Waller's comments. ING considers the move justified.

ING expects housing costs, lower energy prices and weak wage growth to dampen price pressures, so it sees no further hikes.
First time below $4 since mid-July. It should support a subdued November CPI print.

risk_factors: Energy price uncertainty and AI-related investment add to US inflation risk.
Euro and sterling rates may follow US repricing too closely even though the economic backdrop differs.
A hotter-than-expected core CPI path or a 50bp hike, which Waller said he could opt for, would push yields higher.
vol_and_positioning: The 2Y EUR inflation swap fell on the day of the US CPI surprise, which ING reads as euro and sterling rate moves being purely real-rate spillovers.
A US holiday on Wednesday may mean quiet trading.

tension_points.theme: ECB and BoE following the Fed
tension_points.bull_case: Markets assume tighter Fed policy translates into tighter ECB and Bank of England policy, and EUR and GBP rates repriced hawkishly after the US CPI.
tension_points.bear_case: ING says the economic backdrop differs. Higher US rates already tighten European financial conditions, so the ECB or BoE may not need to hike as aggressively as priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: European inflation data, which ING prefers to focus on, coming in hot would undercut ING's view. Oil acting as the common driver would also justify tighter US-Europe correlation.

theme_stances.evidence: markets are already doing the tightening
